questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: Which one of the following is used to produce $\mathrm{Al}$ by electrolysis?
options: Molten $\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+\mathrm{Na}_3 \mathrm{AlF}_6$ electrolyte, carbon coated steel vessel cathode, graphite anode.
Molten $\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+\mathrm{Na}_3 \mathrm{AlF}_6$ electrolyte, graphite cathode, steel anode
questions.solution:
Molien $\mathrm{Al} \mathrm{O}_3+\mathrm{Na} \mathrm{AlF}_6$ as elecurolyse, carbon
coated steel vessel cathode, graphite anode is used to produce aluminium (Al) by electrolysis. The process is called Hall's process.
In this process, purified alumina is mixed with $\mathrm{Na}_3 \mathrm{AlF}_6$ or $\mathrm{CaF}_2$ (cryolite or fluorspar), which lowers the melting point of alumina and brings conductivity.
In the electrolytic cell, steel cathode and series of graphite anode are used.
The overall reaction is
$2 \mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+3 \mathrm{C} \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{Al}+3 \mathrm{CO}_2 \uparrow$
The electrolytic reactions are as follows:
$\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 \mathrmO^{2-}$
At cathode $\quad \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{l})$ At anode $\mathrm{C}(s)+\mathrmO^{2-}($ melt $) \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}(g)+2 e^{-}\mathrm{C}(s)+2 \mathrmO^{2-}($ melt $) \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2(g)+4 e^{-}$
The oxygen liberated at anode reacts with the carbon of anode producing $\mathrm{CO}$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct related to metallurgy?
(A) In electrolytic refining of copper, pure $\mathrm{Cu}$ is used as anode.
(B) Zone refining is based on the principle that impurities are more soluble in the melt than in the solid state of the metal.
(C) $\mathrm{TiI}_4$ upon heating will give pure Ti.
(D) Very pure Zr may be obtained by galvanisation.
(E) In copper smelting, hot air is used to convert to $\mathrm{CuSO}_4$.
The correct answer is
questions.solution:
(B) Zone-refining is based on the principle that impurities are more soluble in the melt than in the solid state of the metal. In this process, a circular mobile heater is used which is fixed at one end of the rod. The rod is made up of the impure metal and convert into pure metallic rod through zone-refining process.
(C) $\mathrm{TiI}_4$ on heating will give pure $\mathrm{Ti}$ at above $1100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ temperature.
$\mathrm{TiI}_4 \xrightarrow{>1100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}} \mathrm{Ti}+2 \mathrm{I}_2$
Thus, option (2) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: What is the slag formed during the extraction of iron?
questions.solution:
Iron is extracted from its ore, (haematite) in a blast furnace. The ore is fed into the top of the furnace along with coke and lime stone.
Carbon monoxide act as reducing agent during the reaction in blast furnace and lime stone decomposes in the hot furnace forming calcium oxide. The molten iron is then tapped from the bottom of the furnace. Further, calcium oxide react with $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ to form a slag.
$\mathrm{CaO}+\mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO}_3$ Slag can be used in making roads.

questions.q: Which element does not exist in elemental state in the earth's crust?
questions.solution:
Out of given four elements C, S, Fe and $\mathrm{Au}$, the non-metals $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{S}$ exist in elemental form as allotropes. $\mathrm{Au}$ is a less active metal. It also exists in nature as elemental form, called nugget.
Fe is an electropositive metal. So, it exists in earth's crust in combined state (compounds), e.g. $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3, \mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4, \mathrm{FeS}_2$ etc.

Fe is an electropositive metal. So, it exists in earth's crust in combined state (compounds), e.g. $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3, \mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4, \mathrm{FeS}_2$ etc.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: What is the role of limestone during the extraction of iron from haematite ore?
questions.solution: During extraction of iron from haematite ore, roasted ore, along with coke and limestone is heated in blast furnance. Here coke behaves as reducing agent and limestone is worked as flux. In this process, in reducing zone $\left(400-900^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\right)$, spongy iron is obtained. In slag zone $\left(900-1200^{{}^{\circ}}\right)$, limestone reacts with impurity (e.g., silica) to form slag. In the combustion and fusion zone $\left(1200-1600^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\right)$, all the charge melts and pig iron is obtained which purified further.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following is not added during the extraction of silver by cyanide process?
questions.solution:
In the extraction of silver from cyanide process (also Mac-Arthur Forrest process), the siliver compound dissolve in $\mathrm{NaCN}$ solution forming a
soluble complex salt, in presence of air, then silver is precipitated from this complex salt by the addition of $\mathrm{Zn}$, because $\mathrm{Zn}$ being more reactive displaces the Ag.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{ S}+4 \mathrm{NaCN} & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ S} \downarrow \\ \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ S}+2 \mathrm{O}_2 & \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \\ 2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+\mathrm{Zn} & \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]+2 \mathrm{Ag} \downarrow\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Zone refining is done for semiconductors and so $\mathrm{A}\rightarrow$ III. Poling is done for metals like $\mathrm{Cu}$ along with other steps like blistering and cupellation. Thus, $\mathrm{B} \rightarrow$ IV.
Liquation is done for metals like $\mathrm{Sn}$ in which it is partially melted and separated. Thus, $\mathrm{C} \rightarrow$ II.
Vapour phase refining is done for metals that form volatile compounds like $\mathrm{Ni}, \mathrm{Ti}, \mathrm{Zr}$, etc. Thus, $\mathrm{D} \rightarrow \mathrm{I}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: Which of the following element is purified by vapour phase refining?
questions.solution: Van Arkel method for refining $Z r, \mathrm{Ti}$ and Mond's process for Ni on vapour phase refining methods.
